claim_audit.qualification: Use the local New York event date, despite the lot page showing a 19 November GMT closing timestamp.

claim_audit.claim: A printed first edition of the final Constitution text from 1787, made for the Convention and Congress
claim_audit.locator: 2021 lot title; 2021 digital catalogue opening paragraphs; retrospective section on the Official Edition
claim_audit.qualification: This was the Goldman copy of the first printing, not the unique handwritten engrossed and signed document. No surviving-copy count is used because sources contain different counts.

claim_audit.claim: More than 17,000 contributors pooled more than US$40 million in Ether, with social-media mobilisation
claim_audit.locator: 2022 Sotheby’s retrospective paragraph on the 2021 ConstitutionDAO campaign
claim_audit.qualification: Deliberately uses supported lower bounds. Dollar valuations varied with the ETH price and the time measured; no exact final fundraising total or final bidder budget is asserted.

claim_audit.claim: Juicebox held the crowdfunding mechanism and PEOPLE allocations corresponded to ETH contributions
claim_audit.locator: Official project redemption statement and original contribution ratio; contemporary development notes’ Juicebox FAQs
claim_audit.qualification: An allocation could be claimed or unclaimed. No claim that each contributor already held transferred tokens, or that tokens represented fractional ownership of the document.

claim_audit.claim: ConstitutionDAO lost and Kenneth Griffin acquired the copy
claim_audit.locator: Project closing statement; Sotheby’s retrospective account of Griffin’s successful bid

claim_audit.claim: Final sale result US$43,173,000 inclusive of Sotheby’s premiums
claim_audit.locator: Official 19 November results roundup: Constitution lot sale-price entry; auction overview results convention
claim_audit.qualification: The exact figure was available in the indexed text of Sotheby’s results article; direct article retrieval timed out. Same-day official press release independently confirms the rounded US$43.2 million result. This is not the hammer price and excludes any applicable taxes and costs.

claim_audit.qualification: The mechanism returned ETH at the contribution ratio. No promise of an identical dollar refund, automatic payment, or recovery of network transaction fees is made.

claim_audit.qualification: Describes the original project’s statement; does not analyse later independent token communities or market activity.

retrieval_limitations: The lot page hides its result behind a login. Public Sotheby’s result reporting was used instead; no login or access-control bypass was attempted.

The exact US$43,173,000 result was retrieved from indexed text of Sotheby’s contemporary results roundup, whose direct page reads timed out. The opened official same-day announcement independently corroborates US$43.2 million rounded.
The original project’s retained closing statement is undated. No exact wind-down date is given in the companion.
No on-chain contribution total or unique-person count was independently reconstructed. The narrative uses Sotheby’s supported lower bounds rather than an exact final dollar total.
release_guardrails: Keep 18 November 2021 as the local event date, with Common rarity and the approved title/caption.
The item is a first-edition printed copy of the Constitution’s final text from 1787, not the unique handwritten engrossed original.
Keep US$43,173,000 inclusive of premiums; do not call it the hammer price or imply taxes and every additional cost are included.
ConstitutionDAO lost. The SOLD screen must never be explained as a successful community purchase.
Do not equate the fundraising total with the available hammer-bid budget or invent a precise reason or numerical breakdown for stopping.
PEOPLE is the contribution-token reference; do not imply ownership of the document or ongoing governance guarantees.
Refunds were offered through an ETH redemption mechanism and were subject to network fees; do not promise automatic or dollar-equivalent full recovery.
Use the four actual visible clues in this order: PEOPLE paddle, SOLD screen, 1787 plaque, printed Constitution.
The room, characters, paddle, plaque and display are interpretive. Do not identify the fictional auctioneer or bidder as a real participant.
The 2022 Sotheby’s retrospective discusses another copy and auction; never import that sale’s date or provenance into the 2021 card.
The exact final art hash must remain 3cdcd2dc96a7a8c03315ddc0217d915b90c7cc81ef04491817dbbb4edff00816.
